quests.sentenceWithBlank: Maria never learned to swim ____ her family lived nowhere near water growing up.
quests.completedSentence: Maria never learned to swim because her family lived nowhere near water growing up.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because' gives the reason she never learned - growing up far from water. 'So' would reverse this, wrongly suggesting not learning to swim caused her to live far from water.
quests.nativeTip: Think about which fact explains WHY she never learned to swim, not something that happened as a result of not swimming.
quests.example: Maria never learned to swim because her family lived nowhere near water growing up.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The bakery ran out of flour by mid-morning, ____ the last few customers left empty-handed.
quests.completedSentence: The bakery ran out of flour by mid-morning, so the last few customers left empty-handed.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So' shows that running out of flour led directly to customers leaving without their orders. 'Because' would reverse this, wrongly suggesting the empty-handed customers caused the flour shortage.
quests.nativeTip: Consider what naturally follows from running out of flour - an effect, not an explanation.
quests.example: The bakery ran out of flour by mid-morning, so the last few customers left empty-handed.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The dog wouldn't go near the vacuum cleaner ____ it associated the noise with a scary thunderstorm months earlier.
quests.completedSentence: The dog wouldn't go near the vacuum cleaner because it associated the noise with a scary thunderstorm months earlier.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because' gives the underlying reason for the dog's fear of the vacuum. 'So' would reverse this, wrongly suggesting the fear caused the earlier thunderstorm association.
quests.nativeTip: This clause explains the dog's fear - a past experience behind the current behavior, not a consequence of it.
quests.example: The dog wouldn't go near the vacuum cleaner because it associated the noise with a scary thunderstorm months earlier.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: ____ the trail map showed a fairly flat route, the hikers found themselves climbing steep switchbacks for most of the afternoon.
quests.completedSentence: although the trail map showed a fairly flat route, the hikers found themselves climbing steep switchbacks for most of the afternoon.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Although' captures the concession between the flat map and the actual steep climbing. 'Whereas' would only fit for comparing two separate, parallel facts, not this kind of broken expectation.
quests.nativeTip: Compare what the map promised with what actually happened on the trail - a mismatch between expectation and reality.
quests.example: although the trail map showed a fairly flat route, the hikers found themselves climbing steep switchbacks for most of the afternoon.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The instructor promised the workshop would run for exactly two hours, ____ it stretched well past three.
quests.completedSentence: The instructor promised the workshop would run for exactly two hours, but it stretched well past three.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'But' captures the gap between the promised two hours and the longer actual time. 'Whereas' would sound too formal for this casual complaint about a workshop running long.
quests.nativeTip: This is a plain, everyday recap of a broken promise - a straightforward contrast, not a formal comparison.
quests.example: The instructor promised the workshop would run for exactly two hours, but it stretched well past three.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The first draft of the mural used mostly cool blues and greens, ____ the final version leaned heavily into warm oranges and reds.
quests.completedSentence: The first draft of the mural used mostly cool blues and greens, whereas the final version leaned heavily into warm oranges and reds.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Whereas' compares these two contrasting color palettes. 'But' would work too but sounds less suited to this precise, descriptive comparison of two versions.
quests.nativeTip: Two different color choices for two different versions of the mural are simply being placed side by side here.
quests.example: The first draft of the mural used mostly cool blues and greens, whereas the final version leaned heavily into warm oranges and reds.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: ____ the committee approves the new bylaws next month, the club will finally be able to open a second location.
quests.completedSentence: if the committee approves the new bylaws next month, the club will finally be able to open a second location.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'If' fits this genuinely uncertain approval process. 'When' would incorrectly suggest the bylaws are certain to be approved.
quests.nativeTip: A committee vote on new bylaws is a process with a real, undetermined outcome, not something bound to happen.
quests.example: if the committee approves the new bylaws next month, the club will finally be able to open a second location.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: ____ the tide drops low enough each afternoon, the fishermen walk out to check their traps on the sandbar.
quests.completedSentence: when the tide drops low enough each afternoon, the fishermen walk out to check their traps on the sandbar.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'When' fits this routine, predictable natural pattern. 'If' would incorrectly suggest doubt about whether the tide will drop each afternoon.
quests.nativeTip: This describes a daily routine tied to the tide - something that reliably happens, not a possibility.
quests.example: when the tide drops low enough each afternoon, the fishermen walk out to check their traps on the sandbar.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The greenhouse tomatoes will need daily watering through the summer ____ the region finally gets its usual rainy season back.
quests.completedSentence: The greenhouse tomatoes will need daily watering through the summer unless the region finally gets its usual rainy season back.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Unless' shows the watering need depends on the rainy season failing to return. 'If' would need 'doesn't get' added to express the same meaning.
quests.nativeTip: Daily watering is needed specifically in the absence of the usual rain - think about which connector already builds that 'not' in.
quests.example: The greenhouse tomatoes will need daily watering through the summer unless the region finally gets its usual rainy season back.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The teacher rearranged the desks into small clusters ____ quieter students would feel comfortable speaking up in smaller groups.
quests.completedSentence: The teacher rearranged the desks into small clusters so that quieter students would feel comfortable speaking up in smaller groups.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So that' introduces this intentional purpose - encouraging quieter students to speak up. 'So' alone would instead describe this as an unplanned effect rather than a deliberate strategy.
quests.nativeTip: Rearranging the desks was a deliberate strategy aimed at a specific social outcome, not an explanation of something already true.
quests.visualAnchor: 🌉 Clause A ──[ so that ]── Clause B
quests.example: The teacher rearranged the desks into small clusters so that quieter students would feel comfortable speaking up in smaller groups.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The desks were rearranged into small clusters, ____ the room now feels much more collaborative during group work.
quests.completedSentence: The desks were rearranged into small clusters, so the room now feels much more collaborative during group work.
quests.grammarRule: Result vs Purpose - so, not so that
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So' introduces this straightforward, observed result. 'So that' would need a forward-looking modal verb to properly express a purpose, which isn't how this sentence is phrased.
quests.nativeTip: This describes the actual, current feeling in the room now - an observed effect, not a stated goal.
quests.example: The desks were rearranged into small clusters, so the room now feels much more collaborative during group work.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The park added motion-sensor lighting along the trail ____ evening joggers could see the path clearly without carrying a flashlight.
quests.completedSentence: The park added motion-sensor lighting along the trail so that evening joggers could see the path clearly without carrying a flashlight.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So that' introduces this intentional purpose, with 'could' expressing the enabled benefit. 'Because' would incorrectly frame this as an explanation rather than a forward-looking goal.
quests.nativeTip: Adding the lighting was a deliberate improvement made with a clear future benefit for joggers in mind.
quests.visualAnchor: 🌉 Clause A ──[ so that ]── Clause B
quests.example: The park added motion-sensor lighting along the trail so that evening joggers could see the path clearly without carrying a flashlight.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The violinist switched to a smaller instrument for the recital ____ the concert hall's acoustics made the full-size version sound too overpowering in rehearsal.
quests.completedSentence: The violinist switched to a smaller instrument for the recital because the concert hall's acoustics made the full-size version sound too overpowering in rehearsal.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because' gives the reason for switching instruments. 'So' would reverse this, wrongly suggesting the switch caused the acoustics problem.
quests.nativeTip: This clause explains the reason for the switch - something discovered in rehearsal, not a consequence of the switch.
quests.example: The violinist switched to a smaller instrument for the recital because the concert hall's acoustics made the full-size version sound too overpowering in rehearsal.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The east side of the vineyard produces grapes with a noticeably sweeter flavor profile, ____ the west side, shaded for much of the afternoon, yields grapes with sharper acidity.
quests.completedSentence: The east side of the vineyard produces grapes with a noticeably sweeter flavor profile, whereas the west side, shaded for much of the afternoon, yields grapes with sharper acidity.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Whereas' compares these two contrasting flavor profiles. 'Although' would suggest the west side yields sharper grapes despite some obstacle, which isn't the relationship here.
quests.nativeTip: Two different sides of the vineyard with two different flavor outcomes are simply being placed side by side.
quests.example: The east side of the vineyard produces grapes with a noticeably sweeter flavor profile, whereas the west side, shaded for much of the afternoon, yields grapes with sharper acidity.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The old clock tower had been silent for nearly a decade, its mechanism rusted and forgotten, ____ on the morning of the town's centennial, it chimed exactly on the hour.
quests.completedSentence: The old clock tower had been silent for nearly a decade, its mechanism rusted and forgotten, although on the morning of the town's centennial, it chimed exactly on the hour.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Although' shows the concession between the years of silence and the sudden, well-timed chiming. 'Because' would incorrectly suggest the silence caused the chiming.
quests.nativeTip: A silent, forgotten clock suddenly chiming on an important morning is the unexpected turn here.
quests.example: The old clock tower had been silent for nearly a decade, its mechanism rusted and forgotten, although on the morning of the town's centennial, it chimed exactly on the hour.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The chef tasted the sauce one more time ____ sending the plate out to the table.
quests.completedSentence: The chef tasted the sauce one more time before sending the plate out to the table.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Before' places the final taste-check earlier than sending the plate out. 'After' would reverse the order, suggesting the plate is sent out first.
quests.nativeTip: This describes the chef's final check as the last step prior to serving, not a condition or an ongoing wait.
quests.example: The chef tasted the sauce one more time before sending the plate out to the table.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The kids built an elaborate sandcastle ____ their parents dozed off under the umbrella nearby.
quests.completedSentence: The kids built an elaborate sandcastle while their parents dozed off under the umbrella nearby.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'While' shows two ongoing actions happening simultaneously. 'Before' or 'after' would suggest one action finished before the other began, which isn't the picture here.
quests.nativeTip: Building a sandcastle and dozing off happen at the same time here, as parallel ongoing activities.
quests.example: The kids built an elaborate sandcastle while their parents dozed off under the umbrella nearby.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The whole neighborhood lost power for a few hours ____ the storm passed through late last night.
quests.completedSentence: The whole neighborhood lost power for a few hours after the storm passed through late last night.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'After' shows the outage followed the storm passing through. 'While' would suggest the outage happened during the storm itself, which the sentence doesn't quite say.
quests.nativeTip: The power outage is described as following the storm, not happening at the same time as it or before it.
quests.example: The whole neighborhood lost power for a few hours after the storm passed through late last night.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: Can't really afford the trip right now ____ I'm still tempted to just book it anyway.
quests.completedSentence: Can't really afford the trip right now though I'm still tempted to just book it anyway.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Though' fits this casual, conversational tone naturally. 'Although' means the same thing but sounds a touch more formal for this kind of relaxed admission.
quests.nativeTip: The casual phrasing and tone here point to a relaxed, spoken-style message between friends.
quests.example: Can't really afford the trip right now though I'm still tempted to just book it anyway.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: Forty-two percent of respondents in the pilot city favored the new policy, ____ only twenty-six percent in the comparison city expressed similar support.
quests.completedSentence: Forty-two percent of respondents in the pilot city favored the new policy, whereas only twenty-six percent in the comparison city expressed similar support.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Whereas' suits this formal, statistical register well. 'But' would sound less suited to this precise, report-style comparison.
quests.nativeTip: The precise percentages and comparison-city framing point to a formal report - the most formal comparison connector fits.
quests.example: Forty-two percent of respondents in the pilot city favored the new policy, whereas only twenty-six percent in the comparison city expressed similar support.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: I'm forwarding this email to you directly ____ the original sender left the company last month.
quests.completedSentence: I'm forwarding this email to you directly because the original sender left the company last month.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because' fits this everyday professional explanation. 'Since' would sound slightly more formal than needed for a routine email forward like this.
quests.nativeTip: The plain, direct tone here points to an everyday professional message, not a formal report or literary account.
quests.example: I'm forwarding this email to you directly because the original sender left the company last month.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The negotiations had collapsed twice before, and neither side seemed willing to budge on the core terms, ____ a deal was somehow signed by the end of the week.
quests.completedSentence: The negotiations had collapsed twice before, and neither side seemed willing to budge on the core terms, although a deal was somehow signed by the end of the week.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Although' shows the concession between the earlier collapses and the eventual signed deal. 'Because' would incorrectly suggest the earlier failures caused the signing.
quests.nativeTip: A signed deal despite two earlier collapses and clear stubbornness is the unexpected turn here.
quests.example: The negotiations had collapsed twice before, and neither side seemed willing to budge on the core terms, although a deal was somehow signed by the end of the week.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The community pool will close for the season this weekend ____ the current warm spell continues for another two full weeks.
quests.completedSentence: The community pool will close for the season this weekend unless the current warm spell continues for another two full weeks.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Unless' shows the closure depends on the warm spell failing to continue. 'If' would need 'doesn't continue' added to express the same meaning.
quests.nativeTip: Staying open happens specifically when the warm spell does NOT end - which connector already includes that 'not'?
quests.example: The community pool will close for the season this weekend unless the current warm spell continues for another two full weeks.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The original bakery location relies almost entirely on walk-in foot traffic, ____ the newer branch across town does most of its business through delivery apps.
quests.completedSentence: The original bakery location relies almost entirely on walk-in foot traffic, whereas the newer branch across town does most of its business through delivery apps.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Whereas' compares these two contrasting business models. 'Although' would suggest the newer branch relies on delivery despite some obstacle, which isn't the relationship here.
quests.nativeTip: Two different locations with two different ways of doing business are simply being compared here.
quests.example: The original bakery location relies almost entirely on walk-in foot traffic, whereas the newer branch across town does most of its business through delivery apps.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The crew had promised a two-week turnaround ____ the work ultimately stretched on for nearly two months.
quests.completedSentence: The crew had promised a two-week turnaround although the work ultimately stretched on for nearly two months.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Although' captures this concession between the original promise and the much longer actual timeline. 'Whereas' would only fit for comparing two separate, parallel facts, not this kind of broken expectation.
quests.nativeTip: A two-week promise stretching into nearly two months is the frustrating gap here between expectation and reality.
quests.example: The crew had promised a two-week turnaround although the work ultimately stretched on for nearly two months.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The city moved the farmers market to Sunday mornings ____ it wouldn't compete with the Saturday craft fair for the same crowd.
quests.completedSentence: The city moved the farmers market to Sunday mornings so that it wouldn't compete with the Saturday craft fair for the same crowd.

quests.nativeTip: Moving the market to Sunday was a deliberate scheduling choice made to avoid a specific conflict.
quests.visualAnchor: 🌉 Clause A ──[ so that ]── Clause B
quests.example: The city moved the farmers market to Sunday mornings so that it wouldn't compete with the Saturday craft fair for the same crowd.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The negotiations between the two unions continued through the night ____ a tentative agreement was finally reached just before sunrise.
quests.completedSentence: The negotiations between the two unions continued through the night until a tentative agreement was finally reached just before sunrise.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Until' captures this continuous negotiating that stops exactly when an agreement is reached. 'Before' would only mark a single point, missing the sense of an all-night effort.
quests.nativeTip: The negotiations continued without stopping, right up to the moment an agreement was reached - this is about ongoing duration through the night.
quests.example: The negotiations between the two unions continued through the night until a tentative agreement was finally reached just before sunrise.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The photographer switched to black and white for the entire series ____ she felt color was distracting viewers from the emotion in each portrait.
quests.completedSentence: The photographer switched to black and white for the entire series because she felt color was distracting viewers from the emotion in each portrait.

quests.nativeTip: This clause explains the photographer's actual artistic reasoning, not an outcome or a comparison.
quests.example: The photographer switched to black and white for the entire series because she felt color was distracting viewers from the emotion in each portrait.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The restaurant had been fully booked for the entire holiday season, every table reserved weeks in advance, ____ it quietly closed its doors for good the following spring.
quests.completedSentence: The restaurant had been fully booked for the entire holiday season, every table reserved weeks in advance, although it quietly closed its doors for good the following spring.
